_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED (wired automatically by the gen-slices auto-loader). Municipal-fiscal-tier population-priority push, 2026-08-13 (AF/G.23). Guinea-Bissau's only prior node was gw-ine-inhpc (af-grok-synthesis.json, enriched separately this round). This file adds the constitutional local-power framework, a real quantified regional/sectoral revenue-sharing formula (Land Law regulation), and a named-region budget-transfer table — the strongest sub-national fiscal record found for this country. Genuinely thin: the operative municipal FINANCE law (Lei 7/96) and the framework law (Lei 5/96) could not be retrieved in full text (paywalled at vlex.pt, not hosted on FAOLEX or any GW government portal), and multiple independent sources (UNIOGBIS-commissioned annotated Constitution 2019, EU MIP 2021-2027 Annex, World Bank PER) corroborate that Guinea-Bissau's autarquia system has not operationally materialized — the elected municipal tier appears never to have taken office; Bissau's own Câmara Municipal president is government-appointed, not elected.

reports.title: Constituição da República da Guiné-Bissau — Capítulo VI, "Do Poder Local" (Artigos 105.º–118.º)
reports.description: Guinea-Bissau's constitutional chapter establishing the country's local-government tier, verified directly from the FAOLEX-hosted text (chapter heading notes "Nova redacção dada pela Lei Constitucional n°1/96"). Art. 105(1): "A organização do poder político do Estado compreende a existência das autarquias locais, que gozam de autonomia administrativa e financeira." Art. 106 defines the tier: "As autarquias locais são os municípios, secções autárquicas e juntas locais" and "Nos sectores funcionarão os municípios, nas secções administrativas funcionarão as secções autárquicas e nas juntas locais funcionarão as juntas de moradores" — i.e. municípios map 1:1 onto "sectores". Art. 107 sets the territorial hierarchy ("o território nacional divide-se em regiões, subdividindo-se estas em sectores e secções"), deferring "a organização e o funcionamento das regiões administrativas" to ordinary law. Art. 110 grants autarquias "património e finanças próprios" and states "o regime das finanças locais, a estabelecer por lei, deverá visar a justa repartição dos recursos públicos pelo Estado e pelas autarquias locais e a necessária correcção de desigualdades entre as autarquias" — a delegation clause with no numeric formula in the constitutional text itself. Art. 118 grants a further, separately delegated share: "As autarquias locais participam, por direito próprio e nos termos definidos pela lei, nas receitas provenientes dos impostos directos." The ordinary laws these articles delegate to (Lei 5/96, Lei 7/96, Lei 6/97) could not be retrieved in full text this round — see _dropped.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument; text as revised by Lei Constitucional n.º 1/96.

reports.title: Decreto n.º 6/2018 — Regulamento Geral da Lei da Terra, Artigo 94.º ("Participação nas receitas e consignação")
reports.description: Guinea-Bissau's General Regulation of the Land Law, published in the Boletim Oficial (Suplemento) of 27 November 2018 and currently in force, contains a real, quantified revenue-sharing formula for the Imposto Fundiário (land tax) — verified by direct PDF download and pdfplumber extraction of the two-column-layout source. Art. 94(1): "O produto de cobrança do Imposto Fundiário constitui receita do Estado e reverte, nas proporções abaixo indicadas, a favor das seguintes entidades: a) 60% a favor do Tesouro Público; b) 20% a favor das comunidades locais; c) 10% a favor das autoridades administrativas regionais e setoriais; d) 10% a favor das comissões fundiárias." Art. 94(3) further splits the regional/sectoral share: "A repartição de fundos referidos na alínea c) do número 1 entre as autoridades administrativas regionais e setoriais efetua-se na proporção de 25% e 75%, respetivamente." Art. 94(4) restricts the funds' use: "As autoridades administrativas regionais e setoriais devem utilizar os valores resultantes da cobrança do Imposto Fundiário na realização de ações de ordenamento e gestão de território, de infra-estruturas de saneamento básico, abastecimento de água, rede elétrica, rede viária e tratamento de lixo." The beneficiary class named here ("autoridades administrativas regionais e setoriais") is the deconcentrated regional/sectoral administrative tier, not explicitly equated in this text to the constitutionally-defined "autarquias locais" (municípios/secções/juntas) — see _dropped for why no edge is drawn to the Constitution node on this basis alone.
reports.cadence_note: One-off regulatory instrument, in force since 27 November 2018.

reports.title: Orçamento Geral do Estado (OGE) 2022 [Proposta] — Ministério da Administração Territorial e Poder Local, Transferências às Regiões
reports.publisher: Ministério das Finanças da Guiné-Bissau — Direção-Geral do Orçamento (DGO)
reports.description: Guinea-Bissau's FY2022 state budget proposal, sourced from CABRI-SBO's budget-transparency repository (SIGFiP-generated document, footer reads "Editado por: DGO... Editado em: 02/12/2021"), itemizes an identical transfer line for each of the country's eight named administrative regions under Título 11 ("Ministério da Administração territorial e Poder local"), Título 4 ("Transferências"): "6411 - Região de Cacheu ... 8,500 ... / 6412 - Região de Oio ... 8,500 ... / 6413 - Região de Biombo ... 8,500 ... / 6414 - Região de Bolama Bijagós ... 8,500 ... / 6415 - Região de Quinara ... 8,500 ... / 6416 - Região de Tombali ... 8,500 ... / 6417 - Região de Bafata ... 8,500 ... / 6418 - Região de Gabu ... 8,500 ..." (figures in thousand FCFA under "Financiamento Interno"; "Total do Capitulo : 361110201 ... 118,000"). Each of the eight regions (Cacheu, Oio, Biombo, Bolama Bijagós, Quinara, Tombali, Bafatá, Gabú) receives an identical 8,500 thousand FCFA (≈USD 14,000 at 2021-22 rates) — a flat, non-differentiated administrative transfer, not a needs- or population-based formula. Bissau, administered as the "Sector Autónomo de Bissau" rather than as a "região," receives no line in this table. The same figures also appear in the whole-of-government "ANEXO III – Despesa Global" annex of the same document.
reports.cadence_note: Annual state budget (OGE); this edition is the FY2022 proposal ("[PROPOSTA]"), not confirmed as the final enacted text.

_dropped.why: Topically adjacent — Constitution Art. 118 grants autarquias a share of direct-tax revenue "nos termos definidos pela lei", and Imposto Fundiário (land tax) is a direct tax — but Decreto 6/2018 Art. 94 never cites the Constitution by article or law number, and its beneficiary class ("autoridades administrativas regionais e setoriais") is not explicitly equated in the text to the constitutionally-defined "autarquias locais" (municípios/secções/juntas). Per the evidence-strict citation rule, no documented edge is drawn despite the topical relationship.

The OGE 2022 regional-transfer table implements the general delegation Constitution Art. 107(2) makes to ordinary law for regional organisation, but the budget document itself never cites the Constitution by article number in the extracted text — genuine NOT FOUND for a documented citation edge.

_dropped.edge: gw-constituicao-poder-local -> Lei n.º 5/96 (Lei de Bases das Autarquias Locais)
_dropped.why: Constitution Art. 110's delegation ("o regime das finanças locais, a estabelecer por lei") is implemented by name in Lei n.º 5/96 (the framework "Lei de Bases das Autarquias Locais"), whose existence and citation is confirmed via the UNIOGBIS-commissioned annotated Constitution (Faculdade de Direito de Bissau, 2019: "LBAL – L de Bases das Autarquias Locais (L 5/96, de 16-09, publicada no BO 38, de 1996)") and via vlex.pt's title index. Full statutory text is NOT FOUND — not on FAOLEX, not on any Guinea-Bissau government portal, and vlex.pt (https://vlex.pt/source/guine-bissau-colect-nea-legisla-o-administrativa-2169) only exposes a paywalled title list. A real, named, documented lead for a future round.

_dropped.edge: gw-constituicao-poder-local -> Lei n.º 7/96 (Autonomia Financeira e Patrimonial das Autarquias)
_dropped.why: Lei n.º 7/96 is Guinea-Bissau's actual municipal FINANCE law — the presumed source of the concrete revenue formula that Constitution Art. 110 only promises "a estabelecer por lei" — confirmed by title/number/date via the UNIOGBIS annotated Constitution's citation apparatus. This is the single most important missing document for this branch: full text NOT FOUND (same paywall/indexing gap as Lei 5/96). A real, named, documented lead for a future round.

_dropped.edge: gw-constituicao-poder-local -> Lei n.º 6/97 (Lei-quadro da criação de Municípios) / Decreto-Lei n.º 4/96
_dropped.why: These instruments would give the actual list of named municípios (per Constitution Art. 106(2), one per "sector"). Confirmed to exist and numbered via the UNIOGBIS annotated Constitution's citation apparatus, but full text NOT FOUND online. A real, named, documented lead for a future round.

The Municipal Electoral Law's full text is NOT FOUND; only its bibliographic citation was recoverable, via the UNIOGBIS annotated Constitution's glossary: "LEA – L Eleitoral Autárquica (L 4/2015, publicada no Suplemento ao BO 32, de 07-08-2018)". Notably, the law is dated/numbered 2015 but its Boletim Oficial publication (which gives it legal force) is dated 07-08-2018 — a roughly three-year enactment-to-publication gap, a structural-delay signature consistent with the non-implementation pattern this branch has flagged in other countries (e.g. CAR, Somalia).

_dropped.edge: gw-* -> Tribunal de Contas da Guiné-Bissau report itemizing named regions/sectors
_dropped.why: The Court of Accounts site (tribunaldecontas.gw / tcontas.gw) is live and does publish real audit reports — one was downloaded and confirmed ("Relatório n° 03/2021", auditing the Centro de Investigação Pesqueira Aplicada, a national fisheries research institute) — but this and the other listed reports (CECOME, PETROGUIN, COVID-19 funds) audit national public enterprises/institutes, not named sub-national territorial units. No Tribunal de Contas report itemizing named regions or sectors with financial figures was found.

_dropped.edge: gw-* -> primary confirmation that municipal/local elections have never been held
_dropped.why: The strongest available corroboration is the UNIOGBIS-commissioned annotated Constitution (Faculdade de Direito de Bissau, 2019 — quasi-primary: UN-commissioned, authored by Guinea-Bissau's own Law Faculty, not a government agency itself): "A afirmação do carácter unitário do Estado que nele se contém passou a ter de ser relativizada à luz do texto constitucional revisto em 1995, podendo mesmo falar-se a partir daí num Estado unitário descentralizado, mesmo se, no plano dos factos, essa descentralização ainda não se tenha materializado" [decentralization 'has not yet materialized in fact', as of 2019]. News-source corroboration exists (e.g. reporting that Bissau's Câmara Municipal president is 'nomeado' — appointed — by the Council of Ministers rather than elected) but was not independently fetched/verified this round and is excluded as a news-source per the standing evidence rule. No official CNE (Comissão Nacional de Eleições) statement or Boletim Oficial decree explicitly confirming no autárquica election has ever been held was found.

_dropped.edge: gw-* -> Comissão Nacional de Eleições (CNE) site content on municipal elections
_dropped.why: cne.gw returned HTTP 200 with HTML via direct curl (the standard WebFetch tool failed twice, once on a self-signed TLS certificate and once on ROBOTS_DISALLOWED), but the raw HTML was not parsed for election-history content before this round's research budget was exhausted. A genuine lead for a follow-up pass.

_dropped.edge: European Commission MIP 2021-2027 Annex for Guinea-Bissau -> [context, not a corpus node]
_dropped.why: Non-Guinea-Bissau-government EU institutional document, used as corroboration only per the branch's context-fallback rule, not minted as a node or drawn as a load-bearing edge. Directly verified in the extracted PDF text (page 7): "Local administrations do not enjoy organisational and financial autonomy, except Bissau as regards to a few sectors, as the government and the Ministries of Territorial Administration and Infrastructures in particular, retain most of the powers and prerogatives." A results-indicator table (page 21) also records a quantified structural-absence baseline: "(Law/regulation on decentralization and administrative autonomy) 2021: 0 / 2024: a) 2 / 2027: b) 2". Corroborates the token-transfer finding in gw-oge-2022-transferencias-regionais and the non-materialization finding from the UNIOGBIS annotated Constitution.

_dropped.edge: World Bank Guinea-Bissau Public Expenditure Review -> [context, not a corpus node]
_dropped.why: Non-Guinea-Bissau-government document, explicitly disqualified from primary status per the standing evidence rule, included only as permitted context. Education chapter: "The education budget remains largely centralized, with resources at the subnational level limited to the collection of school fees from secondary education... Neither regional directorates nor schools receive any transfers from the central administration... Resource distribution is biased towards the capital, Bissau, which absorbs over 60 percent of public resources but represents only 26 percent of the student population... the student population in Oio receive less than 4 percent of available resources, although it represents 14 percent of the total student population." Independently corroborates the token/near-zero real transfer pattern found in gw-oge-2022-transferencias-regionais from an unrelated sector angle.

_dropped.why: cmbissau-gb.com is a live official Câmara Municipal de Bissau site ("A Câmara Municipal de Bissau é responsável pela administração local, planejamento urbano e desenvolvimento sustentável da cidade"), with a functioning contact/services portal and a specific fee schedule for a land-legalization service ("Fazer um depósito de 15.000 Fcfa, na conta bancária da Câmara Municipal de Bissau"), but no published budget, revenue report, or annual accounts were found on the site. Not minted as a report node (no recurring document, no financial figures beyond a single service fee) — flagged as a real primary-source publishing entity worth a follow-up pass in a future round.
